newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares slip ahead of Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares slip ahead of Fed meeting.

text.p: Danish share prices slipped on Monday in a quiet market awaiting the outcome of this evening's Federal Open Market Committee meeting amid speculation of a further rise in U.S. interest rates.
"There has been very little interest in the (Danish) market, which has been cautious ahead of the FOMC meeting," a dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index closed down 0.42 point, at 167.50, in overall bourse turnover of 1.16 billion crowns. The KFX June future however rose 0.10 point to 167.20 with 365 contracts, each worth 100,000 crowns, traded.
"If U.S. interest rates rise it will be a quiet Wednesday and if rates are unaltered the Danish market will rise," the dealer said.
Leading Tuesday's five gainers on the KFX was shipping group A.P.Moeller, whose D/S Svendborg rose 3,000 crowns to 349,000 crowns. Its D/S 1912 was unchanged at 242,500.
The day's other four gainers were Sophus Berendsen,
up five crowns to 895.00, Tele Danmark, up
one crown to 331.00, Jyske Bank, up one to 549.00
crowns and SAS also up one crown, to 71.00.
